Solid amber (static) Non-urgent fault Low-Medium £50–£600 Flashing amber Active misfire - STOP DRIVING Critical £100–£2,500+ Red light Serious fault - STOP DRIVING Critical £100–£10,000+ Solid amber + no symptoms Minor sensor/emissions issue Low £50–£300 Flashing + loss of power Cat damage risk Critical £500–£2,500+ What this usually means in UK cars The Most Common - and Most Misunderstood - Warning Light The check engine light (EML) can mean anything from a loose fuel cap (£0) to a failing catalytic converter (£500-£2,500). In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified five primary causes: Loose or faulty fuel cap - 20% of cases EVAP system leak. Cost: £0-£30. Oxygen sensor failure - 25% of cases Lambda sensor reading incorrect. Cost: £100-£300. Ignition system failure - 20% of cases Spark plugs, coils, leads. Cost: £60-£220. Catalytic converter failure - 15% of cases Blocked or damaged cat. Cost: £500-£2,500+. MAF sensor / EVAP - 20% of cases Air flow readings incorrect or fuel vapour leak. Cost: £50-£300. 🟡 Solid amber Schedule diagnostic within days. Safe to drive short distances. 🔴 Flashing amber Active misfire. STOP DRIVING IMMEDIATELY 🔴 Red light Serious fault. STOP DRIVING IMMEDIATELY ⚠️ The flashing light danger: If your check engine light is flashing, unburnt fuel is entering the exhaust system and destroying your catalytic converter (£500-£2,500 repair). Get it diagnosed. “A flashing light just means a serious fault - I'll drive carefully.” Flashing = active misfire = fuel destroying your catalytic converter. Stop immediately. “I can just disconnect the battery to reset it.” The ECU stores the fault code. Resetting without diagnosis is pointless. “It's probably the oxygen sensor - expensive fix.” Oxygen sensors are £100-£300. Catalytic converters are £500-£2,500. Don't assume the worst. “The light is on because I need a service.” The service light is different. The EML is for engine faults. Get it checked. Book Emergency Diagnostic The loose fuel cap rule Always Check Your Fuel Cap First 💡 Always check your fuel cap first. A loose cap triggers EVAP codes (P0455/P0457) This is the most common EML trigger (20% of all cases). Tighten the cap and drive for 50 miles The light will usually clear automatically once the ECU confirms system pressure seal. Why this works: The EVAP system monitors fuel vapour leaks A loose cap causes a vapour leak The ECU detects the leak and illuminates the light Tightening the cap seals the leak The light clears after several drive cycles Next step if unresolved: If the light doesn't clear after 50 miles: Book a diagnostic - there's another issue. What happens if you ignore it - Detailed progression From £0 to £2,500+ How delayed action exponentially multiplies repair bills. Symptom Progression Cost Impact Solid amber (sensor) Sensor fails, economy drops £100-£300 → £300-£600 Solid amber (misfire) Misfire worsens, cat damage £60-£220 → £500-£2,500+ Flashing (ignored) Cat destroyed, MOT fail £100-£220 → £500-£2,500+ Flashing (driven) Cat blocked, loss of power £100-£220 → £500-£2,500+ + labour The £2,500 mistake: “The light is flashing but I'll just drive home.” The 5 miles you drive could cost you £2,500 in catalytic converter replacement. What to do next Check, Identify, Diagnose A 3-step actionable sequence for vehicle owners. Step 1: Check the fuel cap Is the fuel cap tight? If loose - tighten it. Drive for 50 miles. What does the check engine light mean? + It means the ECU has detected a fault in the engine or emissions system. It could be minor (fuel cap) or serious (misfire). Can I drive with the check engine light on? + Solid amber - yes, short distances. Flashing or red - no, stop immediately. How much does check engine light diagnosis cost in the UK? + Check engine light diagnosis costs £50-£150 at UK independent garages. This includes reading fault codes. Why is the check engine light flashing? + Active misfire. Unburnt fuel is destroying your catalytic converter. Stop driving immediately. How long does it take for the check engine light to clear after fixing? + 50-100 miles of driving, or the garage can clear it with diagnostic equipment. What's the most common cause of a check engine light? + A loose fuel cap (20% of cases). Always check it first.
